sentences.text: The respondent herein had approached the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh by way of W.P.No.24044 of 2009, contending that Ac.2.36 RRR,J & HN,J cents of land in Sy.No.630 of Valsapalli Revenue Village, Madanapalle Mandal, Chittoor District, belonging to him had been taken away by the appellants herein for the purpose of AVR HNSS project, Madanapalle Unit-1, without acquiring the said land under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 1894 Act) and by seeking to pay ex-gratia amount by treating the respondent herein as an assignee.

3. The case of the appellants was that the land was originally assigned to one Jampala Subbanna,
under a D.K.T patta in the year 1928 and that the respondent herein had acquired the land from the person, who had purchased this land from the said Jampala Subbanna on 04.11.1940.

On this basis,
it was contended that the respondent would also be treated as an assignee to whom the provisions of the A.P. Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977 (for short the Act 9/1977) and the conditions of assignment would be applicable.

entities.text: A.P. Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was contended that since the respondent was to be treated as an assignee he would only be entitled to the ex-gratia amount and nothing more.

4. A learned Single Judge of the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh, by judgment dated 11.11.2010, after hearing both sides, allowed the writ petition with a direction to the appellants herein to treat the respondent herein as the owner of the land and accord compensation under the 1894 Act.

5. The learned Single Judge came to the conclusion that the respondent cannot be treated as an assignee in view of the fact that the land had been assigned to Jamapal Subbanna, in the year 1928 whereas the RRR,J & HN,J condition of non-alienation came to be introduced by way of G.O.Ms.No.1142, dated 18.06.1954 and consequently, the provisions of the Act 9/1977 would be applicable.
6. Aggrieved by this judgment, the appellants have moved the present appeal.

7. The learned Government Pleader for Revenue would contend that once the land is treated as assigned land, sale or purchase of the said assigned land is void under the provisions of the Act 9/1977 in as much as any sale prior or after the Act coming into force was prohibited with the consequences that any such alienation would be rendered null and void and the possession of the land was to be taken back and given to the original assignee or dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
He would submit that the condition of non-alienation is available even before G.O.Ms.No.1142, dated 18.06.1954 had been issued in view of the Board Standing Orders issued prohibiting such alienation.
8. The Act 9/1977 prohibits alienation of land which falls within the ambit of "assigned land".
For the purpose of land to be treated as assigned land, there must be a condition of absolute non-alienation, as required under Section 2(1) of the Act 9/1977.

9. In the present case, it may also be noted that after the condition of non-alienation was introduced in the D.K.T. pattas being issued to the landless poor persons, only in the year 1954, under G.O.Ms.No.1142 dated 18.06.1954.

sentences.text: RRR,J & HN,J land in 1940 under a registered deed of sale which is also before the introduction of G.O.Ms.No.1142 dated 18.06.1954.

10. For all the aforesaid reasons, it must be held that the land in question does not fall within the meaning of assigned land and consequently, the respondent would have to be treated as the pattadar and owner of the said land.
11.
In the circumstances, this writ appeal would have to be dismissed upholding the ratio laid down by the learned Single Judge.

However, the fact remains that the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 which was in force at the time of the judgment being rendered by the learned Single Judge, has now been repealed and replaced by the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short Act 30/2013).

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 12. In the circumstances, this writ appeal is disposed of subject to the modification of the learned Single Judges order to the extent of directing the appellants to pay compensation to the respondent herein in accordance with the Act 30/2013.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
